$comment: Who uses Hifth, what each of them is trying to do, and what proves it still works.
This is the third document in the same family as docs/map.json and
docs/validation/ledger.json, and it answers the question neither of them does.
The map answers 'where do I change this?' — organised by feature, for someone
already inside the code. The ledger answers 'what can a machine not check?'.
This file answers 'what can a person do with this thing, and what would fail
if we broke it?' — organised by actor, in the actor's own words.
WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING SEPARATELY FROM THE MAP: a feature list and a use-case
list disagree in the places that matter. Features are things we built; use
cases are things someone wants. 'editions-and-skins' is one feature and two
unrelated wants. 'Come back to where I was' is one want spread across the
router, the trail beads and the page stage, and it is exactly the kind of
promise that breaks without any single feature looking broken.
WHY EVERY USE CASE CARRIES A `proof`: this is the field the whole file exists
for. A use case with no named test is a claim about the product that nobody
checks — and a document full of unchecked claims is a wish list wearing the
costume of a specification. Naming the test does three things at once: it
tells a reader how to see the behaviour for themselves, it fails the build
when the test is renamed or deleted (scripts/gate-use-cases.mjs), and it makes
an unproven promise impossible to write down quietly. When the proof is
genuinely thinner than the promise, say so in `gap` rather than overstating it
— an honest hole is a to-do, a hidden one is a lie.
The pointers cannot rot. `code[].symbol` and `proof[].test` are checked against
real files on every push and on the commit that renames them, by the same
reader the code map uses (scripts/code-pointers.mjs). Line numbers are never
stored; the renderers compute them at read time.
RENDERERS — one source, three ways to read it:
make use-cases                 one line per use case, grouped by actor
make use-cases ACTOR=<id>      one actor's full picture, with file:line
make use-cases-doc             regenerate docs/use-cases.md (the mermaid map)
The /maintain-use-cases skill drives a session from this file. Never restate a
use case anywhere else; point at the id.
FIELDS
actors[]   id · name (as the actor would be named out loud) · what they are
here to do. An actor with no use cases fails the gate — a name
with nothing behind it is decoration.
useCases[]
id       kebab-case, stable, and phrased as the goal, not the mechanism.
actor    an actor id.
goal     one line, first person, in the actor's words. If it names a
component or a function, it is written from the wrong side.
feature  a feature id in docs/map.json — where to go to change it. This is
the join between the two documents, and it is gate-checked, so a
feature cannot be renamed out from under a use case.
code[]   {file, symbol} — the two or three places this actually happens.
Not the whole path through the code; the map has that.
proof[]  {file, test} for a named test, or {gate} for a named CI gate
(a key in package.json scripts). At least one is required.
includes[] other use-case ids this one contains — UML <<include>>. You
cannot hop without first selecting, so `hop` includes `select`.
gap      optional. What the proof does NOT cover. Rendered in the doc,
deliberately visible, so a thin proof reads as thin.

actors.name: الحافظ · the hafiz
actors.what: Someone memorising the Qur'an, holding a phone, usually mid-revision. Every gesture has to survive being made by a thumb while attention is on the page rather than the app.

actors.name: the validator
actors.what: The person doing what a machine cannot — a phone in one hand, a printed mushaf on the table. Usually the same human as the maintainer, but with a different job and no access to a terminal while doing it.

actors.name: the maintainer
actors.what: Whoever is changing the app next, including this project's own future self. Arrives cold, needs to find the right layer, and must not be able to break a promise silently.

actors.name: CI
actors.what: The automated judge. An actor rather than scenery: several promises here are kept by a gate refusing a commit, and nothing else keeps them.

a bare page link moves the stage, not just the header

useCases.goal: I know where I want to be — البقرة ٢٥٥ — take me there without turning pages.

proof.test: `/` opens the jumper and a jump lands like a link
a jump to an un-vendored ayah is refused, not faked

useCases.goal: Move to the next page the way a mushaf moves — right to left — and be told honestly when there is no next page.

proof.test: arrows turn pages, and stop honestly at the ends of the book
a sideways flick turns the page, and the band tracks the finger
a page that would not load is said, not silently swapped for another

useCases.goal: Get from where I am to somewhere far away in the book by dragging, and know before I let go where I will actually land.

proof.test: spans the printed mus'haf and says how much of it is here
letting go in the gap lands on the nearest page we have, and says so
commits on release, not on every value the thumb passes over

useCases.goal: When I open this on a laptop, show me the mus'haf the way it is bound — two pages facing each other, the earlier one on my right — instead of one page floating in a field of empty.

proof.test: puts the lower page number on the right
appears above the breakpoint and does not exist below it
puts the lower page number on the right
still turns pages with the arrow keys the header advertises

useCases.gap: Only the desktop project ever renders a spread, and it runs one file. The rest of the suite — every aria snapshot, every golden image, the axe pass — is recorded on a phone, so a regression that only shows at desktop width has exactly these four assertions standing between it and a release. Nothing checks how a spread behaves under pan and zoom, where two mounted pages share a frame budget that was measured with one.

useCases.goal: Do not show me a blank sheet of paper and let me think page 8 is empty. Tell me it is not in this build.

proof.test: announces the missing facing page instead of showing blank paper
draws the missing facing page as absent, not as blank paper
leaves the far side blank and unlabelled at the end of an odd-length print
puts the lower page number on the right

useCases.goal: On a screen with room, stop making me open a sheet to change the language, and tell me the keyboard can turn pages.

proof.test: gives the header the controls the phone had to hide
only hints keys that actually do the thing the hint claims
no horizontal overflow, and a constant header height, from 320 to 430

useCases.gap: The keyboard hint is `aria-hidden`, so a screen-reader user is still told nothing about the shortcuts — they are reachable and labelled individually, but there is no equivalent of the legend. Whether that is right is open question ④ in docs/design/desktop.md.

useCases.goal: Tell me what I can do here the first time, and then never again.

proof.test: the coach marks teach three verbs once, then never again

useCases.goal: Colour the rules while I revise, and take the colour away again without moving a single glyph.

proof.test: switching on marks ayahs with their rules
plain → tajweed → plain leaves the page geometry byte-identical

useCases.goal: Use the mushaf my eyes know, and be told plainly which ones do not exist yet rather than shown a substitute.

proof.test: the mushaf picker shows what exists and why the rest does not

useCases.goal: Open it in a masjid basement, on a plane, a week after I last used it, and have it just work.

proof.test: a visited page still opens with the network offline
an offline hop lands on a page whose SVG was cached alongside it
an evicted shell is rebuilt, so offline still works afterwards

useCases.gap: Everything here is a headless browser with the network switched off. Whether a real phone's OS evicts the cache over eight days is the one thing these cannot answer — that is docs/validation/ledger.json → offline-survival-8-day.

useCases.goal: Say which juz I am revising, keep the whole of it on this phone before I leave, and be told — in words, while I still have signal — if the phone ever takes it back.

proof.test: opens a page the reader has never visited, with the network gone
a sweep is said out loud, and the juz can be put back
a pack the sweep only half took is not left looking kept
a swept pack is named as incomplete, not left looking kept

useCases.gap: The promise is about a phone a week from now, and the tests take the storage themselves, at once, on demand. A real sweep chooses its own moment and may not take everything — docs/validation/ledger.json → offline-survival-8-day is the check that watches one happen, and it is the reason `torn` is a state rather than a rounding error.

useCases.goal: Keep a private record of what I have actually opened, see it — which pages, hizb or juz have gone weeks without me — and press the one that has waited longest to open it.

proof.test: answers with the most recent day, whatever order the log is in
knows its own age before a single look is recorded
does not record the second tap that dismisses a selection
credits the source of a hop, never the ayah the app moved them to
draws absent as a different kind of thing from cold, not a paler one
opens the division when its cell is pressed, and gets out of the way
offers no control on a cell with no paper behind it
a tap on an ayah is still on the map after a reload
pressing a hizb on the map opens it
a wiped record reads as a young record, not as an empty one

useCases.gap: Two holes, and the first is not closable in this repo. iOS deletes script-writable storage after seven days of no interaction, which is precisely the history this promise is about. The e2e can take the record with one CDP call and prove the map still says how old it is, but it cannot wait eight days on a real phone — that is docs/validation/ledger.json → offline-survival-8-day. Second, the marquee path is proven at the store, not through the gesture: no unit test drives a real drag, so «one look, not twelve» is asserted on `recordLook` rather than on a release over twelve ayahs. Loop 4b closed the third hole this entry used to carry: the map drew two held hizb and fifty-eight absent ones, so it was a picture of an inventory rather than of a mus'haf. It is sixty of sixty now, and the absent treatment is held by a trimmed manifest instead of by the build. A fourth is new with the press: the grid's ArrowUp/ArrowDown ask the browser how many cells fit on a row, and in jsdom every `offsetTop` is 0, so the unit suite proves the sideways walk and the browser proves the rest — the vertical step is asserted nowhere, and would degenerate to Home/End without failing a test.

useCases.goal: Reach every ayah, every hop and every control with a screen reader or a keyboard, hearing words rather than glyphs.

proof.test: keyboard-only: focus an ayah, select with Enter, open rail, hop, land
the mushaf page is a labelled group of ayah buttons
the chrome announces every control by word, never by glyph

useCases.gap: axe and aria snapshots check the tree, not the experience. Whether VoiceOver's rotor actually gets a hafiz through a hop is ledger check screen-reader-walkthrough.

useCases.goal: Let me drive the app in English if that is the language I think in — without turning the mus'haf itself into something it is not.

proof.test: an English phone opens an English chrome
the switch is in the colophon, and the choice survives a reload
the mus'haf, the rail, the trail and the page bar stay right-to-left
leaves no Arabic in the English chrome

useCases.gap: Two languages, and the second one is the author's second language. Nothing here judges whether the English reads well to a hafiz who uses it — only that it is English, complete, and has not leaked into the places that must stay Arabic.

useCases.goal: When the app counts something in Arabic, let it count the way Arabic counts — «صفحتان», «٣ صفحات», «١٠٣ صفحات» — instead of the nearest thing a ternary could manage.

proof.test: agrees with the plural rules of the language, not with a ternary
writes counts inside aria-labels in the language's own digits

useCases.gap: Only `distance` is stated as a plural. Seven other Arabic messages still write one fixed form for every count — «٣ روابط» is right, «١١ روابط» is not. They are one JSON edit each now, and each wants a hafiz's eye. docs/design/i18n.md §⑨.

useCases.goal: Give the app a third language by writing that language, not by re-typing 134 interface members and hoping I got the plural rules right.

proof.test: builds a bundle for every locale that has a catalog
carries the same keys in every language
gives each language the digits it declared

useCases.gap: Proven at two locales. The checklist in docs/design/i18n.md §⑦ is written for someone who has not read the conversation, but nobody has walked it end to end for a third language yet.

useCases.goal: Refuse to ship a locale that is missing a key, whose plurals are incomplete, or whose generated code was never regenerated — rather than let English words appear inside an Arabic sheet.

proof.test: carries the same keys in every language

useCases.gap: The gate checks that every category is handled, not that the words inside each category are right. «صفحتان» in the `few` slot would pass. Only a reader of the language catches that.

useCases.goal: Tell me whose mushaf this is and under what terms, without making me hunt for it.

proof.test: every source whose licence asks to be named is named, with its link
the wordmark opens the source offer for this build

useCases.goal: Do the check that needs a phone or a printed mushaf, following instructions on the device I am holding.
useCases.gap: The gate proves every outstanding check has a followable runbook and that the phone guide was regenerated. It cannot prove the runbook's Expect lines match what the phone shows — only walking it does, which is the point of walking it.

useCases.goal: Record what I found in one line, and be told immediately what that verdict now obliges us to build.
Arrive cold and find the entrypoint of the thing I have been asked to change, without grepping.
See every promise this app makes, whose promise it is, and which test would fail if I broke it.
Regenerate the mutashabihat shards and know the output is the same as anyone else would have produced.
useCases.gap: The gate proves an edge shares words with its source — it cannot prove the pair is a mutashabih a hafiz would recognise, and it does not score shared-root edges at all. That is ledger check edge-spot-audit, against a printed mushaf; `make validate` prints which classes of edge no human has ever looked at.

useCases.goal: Add pages to the corpus and have the polygons stay clickable and the glyphs stay outlines.
Before publishing, know the GPL source offer resolves for a stranger — not just for me, signed in.

proof.test: the wordmark opens the source offer for this build

useCases.gap: `source-offer` is run on demand, not by CI on every commit — it reaches the public internet, and a check that can go red because GitHub is having a bad morning teaches everyone to ignore red. It is red today for a real reason: the repository is private, so the offer 404s anonymously (task #53). And nothing watches the deployed build, because there is not one yet — `--url` exists and is tested, but has never been pointed at a live deploy.

useCases.goal: Fail a commit that moves the paint on the page, including the differences no DOM assertion can see.
useCases.gap: The images are the gate; these two scripts only keep the harness honest (right browser, sane file sizes). The pictures themselves are judged by `make golden`, which is not a gate a script can stand in for.

useCases.goal: Fail a commit where a vendored source loses its licence, or the app tells a reader something SOURCES.md does not say.
Fail the commit that renames a symbol out from under a document, on the commit that does the renaming.
Fail a commit that changes what a shared link means without saying so in the catalog a teacher's link is judged by.

proof.test: does NOT reject an unreadable field= — the link still names the ayah

useCases.gap: It checks that the three renderings of the grammar agree — parsed, emitted, documented, and the documented failure mode matching what the parse branch actually does. It cannot check that the prose in the 'what it does' column is true, only that a row exists.

useCases.goal: Fail a commit that pushes the JS past what a mid-tier phone on a slow connection can afford.
